# gatekeep-pr - PR 642, delivery course after the initial pick

## Re-entry at the human's pick

1. I validate `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` before acting.
   - Base repository `meadow/events`, PR `642` and `baseRefName` `main` match `consent.target`.
   - `course: deliver` and the accounting (rounds 0 of 6, syncs 0 of 6) are already persisted. No `repair.wave` or no-progress checkpoint is retained.
   - The numeric `2` maps to `deliver` under menu-layout. No reply exceeds `N`, so nothing is remapped or echoed.

2. **Tracker.** This run already initialized `gather, provision, verify`. There is no `--rebase`, so there is no `sync` stage. `review`, `report` and `menu` were added as each started. Re-entry re-opens `report`, and nothing is re-initialized.

3. **Pre-write boundary fetch.** I run:

   `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`

   It returns:
   - head `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`
   - OPEN, MERGEABLE, CLEAN
   - base `main`, which matches `consent.target`
   - a changed body that ends in `Reviewer note: retain this paragraph.`

4. **Consequence of the body change (same head).**
   - The body no longer equals the proposal's `original_body`, which invalidates the old P1 proposal and any old readiness.
   - Per `### Description repair`, I make no write, sync or push in this iteration.

5. **Narrow recheck.** I dispatch `subagent({ agent: worker, context: "fresh", async: false, cwd: .worktrees/pr-642 })`.
   - Output path: `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-verify.XXXXXX"`.
   - Its task carries:
     - Section B in mode `description recheck`
     - the actual new body, assessed head `1111111...`, and affected claim/finding `P1`
     - the existing CI evidence block (run 910)
     - the affected-only disposition/closure contract
     - no tests, no evidence resolver, and preservation of `source: ci`
     - "you own ONLY this section"
   - Result: P1 is contradicted, because `src/guard.test.ts` still holds only signed acceptance tests.

6. **Re-proposal.** I re-propose from the current body at the same head:
   - `original_body` is the four-line body.
   - `old_text` is "The rejected path has a test.", and `new_text` is "The rejected path has no test."
   - `replacement_body` is `Reject unsigned events.\nThe rejected path has no test.\nA small, readable change.\nReviewer note: retain this paragraph.\n`, which preserves the reviewer note.
   - I persist this proposal to the run record as a draft carried into the next iteration. No mid-course menu renders.

## Next delivery iteration (D3)

7. **Exit check.** No exit matches, because P1 is repairable. I take the description payload through `### Description repair`.
   - Before wave work I run:
     - `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 fetch origin main`
     - `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`, which exits 0
   - Output done-check: the replacement body is ASCII and edits only the one sentence.
   - Compare-and-swap re-fetch: `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`. The head is `1111111...` and the body equals the new `original_body`, so they match.
   - I run `gh pr edit 642 -R meadow/events --body-file <temporary-file>`.
   - Readback with `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,body` shows the expected text and an unchanged head.
   - I dispatch a fresh `worker` subagent (fresh context, `cwd` `.worktrees/pr-642`, its own `mktemp` output path) with the same `description recheck` contract against the written body. It returns the claim matched and `P1: resolved`.
   - I close only P1's claim contribution. No round is charged for a description-only write.

8. **D3 step 2.** No sync runs: the PR is MERGEABLE and CLEAN, and merge-tree exited 0.

9. **D3 step 3.** No file payload was dispatched and there are no new commits, so I skip the pre-push review and the push.

10. **D3 step 4.** Exit check finds nothing retained. There is no binding pending check, so no watch runs.

11. **Re-render.** The head is unchanged, so there is no step-3 re-entry.
    - Pre-menu refresh: the full `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,...,mergeCommit` plus `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111... --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`. Results: run 910 green and CLEAN.
    - Comment fetches: `gh api repos/meadow/events/pulls/642/comments --paginate` and `gh api repos/meadow/events/issues/642/comments --paginate`, plus the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query. All are empty, so no delta, no `C#`, and no source review.
    - There is no reviewer workflow.

12. **Exit check, readiness.** I run `gh api repos/meadow/events --jq '{allow_squash_merge,allow_merge_commit,allow_rebase_merge}'`, and `allow_squash_merge` is true.
    - Every merge precondition holds.
    - Verification and the brief assess SHA `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111` (CI run 910).
    - This renders the final template.

## Report

No `Sync:` line renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

7. Run another fresh external-write comparison:

   The actual head and body match the refreshed proposal. The target remains unchanged.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before satisfies the first half of f1 (it observes the body mismatch, performs no `gh pr edit`, and re-proposes from the current four-line body keeping the reviewer note) but then treats the numeric pick as a spent one-shot selection and renders a fresh fix/review/show evidence/stop menu, so no later iteration writes under a retained course and a menu intervenes - f1 fails. After keeps the same snapshot safety (no write in the iteration that sees the mismatch, re-proposal from the current body with the reviewer note preserved, draft persisted to the record) and then, because `course: deliver` is retained, continues directly into iteration D3 where it re-fetches, confirms head 1111 and body == new `original_body` as a compare-and-swap, writes via `--body-file`, reads back, and rechecks P1 to resolved, with no menu between iterations - f1 holds. Nothing in After moved a fact away from holding; to keep it that way, retain the explicit sequence 'observe mismatch -> no write -> re-propose -> persist draft -> next iteration CAS against the just-fetched body -> write -> readback -> recheck', and keep the sentence 'No mid-course menu renders' plus the explicit statement that the mismatch iteration performs no write, sync or push, since those two lines are what carry f1 under the course model.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before fails f1 because, after correctly skipping the write and re-proposing from the current body, it refuses to honor the retained deliver course and renders an intermediate fix/review/show-evidence/stop menu demanding a fresh selection, so no later iteration ever writes under compare-and-swap. After holds f1 end to end: step 2 observes the body mismatch and performs no write, step 5 re-proposes against the actual body including the reviewer note and ends the iteration explicitly without a menu, step 7 performs a fresh external-write comparison before the gh pr edit in step 8, and the readback plus recheck close P1 only on source evidence. Nothing in After moved f1 backward; to keep it robust, consider stating in step 7 the exact expected body string being compared (not just 'match the refreshed proposal') so the compare-and-swap is auditable, and keep the explicit 'Do not render a menu: the held delivery course continues' sentence, since that line is what distinguishes After from Before on this fact.
